t.E577.agn: In 1998 JECFA set a group ADI 'not specified' for glucono delta-lactone and the calcium, magnesium, potassium and sodium salts of gluconic acid. JECFA reported that single doses of glucono delta-lactone above 20 g have a laxative effect in humans and that diarrhoea has been reported in volunteers taking 20–50 g per day. EFSA's re-evaluation in the EU is ongoing (a new call for data was issued in 2023).
t.E577.body: Gluconic acid and its salts are normal intermediates formed in the body during the breakdown of glucose via the pentose phosphate pathway; part of the ingested gluconate is excreted unchanged in urine and the rest is broken down.
t.E577.found.0: In the EU, may be used in many foods at quantum satis (as much as needed)
t.E577.prod: Produced by neutralising with potassium hydroxide gluconic acid obtained by electrolytic or chemical oxidation of glucose or by fermentation with the mould Aspergillus niger.
t.E577.regx.0: Group ADI 'not specified' for glucono delta-lactone and gluconate salts.
t.E577.regx.1: Group I additive; generally authorised at quantum satis (as much as needed).
t.E577.regx.2: Re-evaluation ongoing; a call for data was issued in 2023 (deadline 31.03.2024).
t.E577.summary: The potassium salt of gluconic acid. Used as an acidity regulator.
t.E577.what: The potassium salt of gluconic acid, used as an acidity regulator.
